items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: He'd go off and stay an hour and a half and, oh, I was in heaven. And they had Denzil Best on drums, Al McKibbon on bass and Monk on piano.

ctx.x: I wonder, you knew Coleman Hawkins when he was playin' regularly on 52nd Street.

Yes, well everybody knew he was my idol and I dressed like him, I played like him and I had a moustache like him. And, you know, I was there all the time. So one night he said, "I think I'll play 'Body and Soul' in E natural." So I says, "O.K.". And we played it and he laughed and he said, after that, that I was his boy, you know what I mean. Every time I come in there, if he wanted to go somewhere he say, "Go on up there, 'cause they think you're me anyway." He'd go off and stay an hour and a half and, oh, I was…

his shoes were hand made and all of his suits were made, his shirts were made. And he was just a classy person, yeah. And he always had a new car every year and he always had fresh horns. He only kept a horn about six or eight months, then he'd get a new one. So I says, "Why you do that?" He says, "Well, son, you gotta always keep your horn fresh." And I never forgot that.
